title: Rødgrød (Red Fruit Porridge)
description: Prepared with juice, sago or flour or rice flour or grains, and cream.

ingredients.name: Thickening agent: 4 1/2 ounces sago flour, or 1/2 pound rice flour, or 1 pound sago grains
Cold sweet cream or creme for serving
Optional: A small handful of scalded and finely crushed almonds (some bitter)

steps: For the best Rødgrød, use 3 pots of black currant juice and 1 pot of raspberry juice, placed over heat to boil.
When boiling, add the thickening agent (mixed with a little of the cold juice) to the pot and cook with continuous stirring for 6 to 8 minutes; cooking is shortest with sago flour.
Before ladling the porridge into large flat bowls, test if it is stiff enough by placing a teaspoon on a saucer and setting it in cold water.
If the porridge is too thin, add a little more thickening agent; if too thick, thin it with boiling water.
Serve with cold sweet cream or creme and sprinkled vanilla sugar.
Alternatively, add a small handful of scalded and finely crushed almonds, including some bitter ones.

Other options for juice: exclusively black currant (from 3 pounds berries) or 2 pounds cherries and 1 pound black currant. For cooking the fruit, use 1 pot of water for each pound of fruit; from 3 pounds of berries, 4 pots of juice are obtained after straining.

title: Rødkaal (Red Cabbage)

steps: Remove the outer leaves and cut the cabbage in quarters and slice into fine strips, without including any of the core.

title: Rødvins-Sauce til Steg (Red Wine Sauce for Roast)
description: A sauce made with red wine, wheat flour, and meat.
steps: Brown a piece of butter in a roasting pan, but not too strongly
Add 2 tablespoons wheat flour and rub it out with the back of a spoon
Continue moving it from one spot in the pan to another so it does not rest long enough to burn
Keep the heat from being too strong under the pan
When it has acquired a nice brown color, gradually add meat broth and skimmings from the roast
The broth does not need to be very strong if you have skimmings
When this is mixed a few times but still too thick, add red wine until it becomes the desired thickness
Add chopped onions, chopped anchovies, a little stirred mustard, pickled oyster sauce to taste, and a little pepper
Cook all this well and then strain it
Place the sauce back in the pan to heat it and add a little soy sauce

If the roasting pan is only iron and not well mixed with steel, do not keep the wine in the pan, but when the sauce is mixed with broth, place it in a small tinned copper pan or glazed pot and prepare it there
This sauce is suitable for beef roast and can also be used for mutton roast; for goose, duck, and ham roast use more mustard

title: Saltede Snittebonner (Salted String Beans)
description: Prepared with beans and salt.
steps: The beans must be freshly picked so they are fresh and crisp. Dry them in a cloth, remove the strings and cut them finely.

In a crock spread a thin layer of salt, then a layer of beans about three fingers thick, then a layer of salt thick enough to cover the beans, then beans, and so forth; press each layer firmly and the last must be salt
Cover with a piece of cloth, place a disk on top and on this a fairly heavy weight, which after some time, when the beans have become firm, can be removed
Tie the crocks, place them in a dry spot and they will keep until summer
When they are to be used, put them with the salt in sufficiently much boiling water and cook until tender, then strain through a sieve where the water is pressed out well, and stew them

If the beans, which is especially the case in early spring, should be too salty when the water is pressed from them, they can be placed for a short time in cold water with a little powdered sugar in it

The beans can also be salted whole in the same way after they are dried and have the strings removed. By adding a little prepared soda to the water in which the beans are cooked, they become tender quickly

Pour the soup into the tureen and serve with lemon slices.

Sauté this in a slice of butter, then stir in a little red wine, a couple of egg yolks along with salt and pepper.
Spread this forcemeat on slices of French bread from which the crust has been removed and which have been fried in butter in a pan.
Place these in a well-heated oven so the forcemeat bakes quickly.

title: Soya (Soy Sauce)
description: A sauce made with meat, white pepper, and onions.
steps: Place 3 liters (3 pots) good meat broth over the fire and bring to a boil, skim well and strain through a fine cloth once it has finished skimming.
Dilute the broth with so much water that it becomes appropriately salty.
Return 3 L (3 pots) of this to the pot along with 3 teaspoons ground white pepper, 1 teaspoon paprika, 1 teaspoon ginger, 1 teaspoon cloves, 2 chopped red onions and 3 bay leaves.
Simmer the broth with these ingredients for at least 3 quarters of an hour and strain again.

While the soy sauce is cooking, brown 1/4 kg (1 1/2 s) powdered sugar in a pan and add it to the hot soy sauce to give it color. The sugar must be dark brown, but not burnt, as it can otherwise easily give a bad taste.
Finally add 1/2 bottle sherry.
If it is preferred to have the soy sauce smooth, stir potato starch in some of the wine and bring the soy sauce to a boil again.

Boil slowly for one Hour, and skim properly.

title: Spegepølser (Smoked Sausages)
description: Prepared with meat, beef, and saltpeter.

ingredients.name: 6 pounds fresh beef from the inner loin
3-4 pounds pork fat, cut into small cubes

steps: Mince the lean meat and beef very finely
Place in a trough and knead with hands for ½ hour
Add 2 pounds salt, 1½ ounces ground saltpeter, ½ ounce ground pepper, ½ ounce ground allspice and ½ ounce ground cloves
Knead again for ½ hour and spread in the trough
Add 3-4 pounds pork fat cut into small cubes and pour in 5 bottles of red wine
Knead thoroughly
Use the widest and thickest ox intestines, cleaned and prepared like pork intestines
Sew one end closed and place in lukewarm water
Stuff very tightly so that no empty spaces remain
After stuffing, rub well with salt and keep for 24 hours
Then pack the sausage meat more tightly together and tie the end with twine to form a loop for hanging in smoke
Let lie another 24 hours, then dry off, wrap in thin paper and hang in smoke for 14 days
Then hang in a dry place
Do not make smoked sausages unless you are certain of having completely trichinosis-free meat

title: Stegt Kalkun (Roasted Turkey)
description: Prepared with turkey, liver, and heart.
steps: Slaughter the turkey 3 to 4 days before use.
Pluck, singe, and cut up the turkey.
Remove the innards and wash thoroughly.
Blanch in boiling water for 2 minutes, then wash in cold water.
Rub inside with salt and pepper.
Place the cleaned liver under one wing and the cleaned, prepared gizzard under the other, unless they are to be used for stuffing.
Tie the legs together over the rump.

For bread stuffing: remove the crust from an old French bread, soak in sweet milk, squeeze out the milk, let stand for one hour, then mix with 3 eggs, 2 tablespoons washed currants, salt, pepper, sugar, half a quarter pound of softened butter, and finely chopped liver.
For alternative stuffing: scrape the liver, gizzard, and heart, chop 4 anchovies, 2 lemons, and a French bread soaked in water, add 1 tablespoon flour, pepper, salt, and 2 eggs.

title: Stikkelsber-Grod (Gooseberry Jelly)
description: Prepared with gooseberries, corn, and water.
steps: If the berries are unripe and very sour, they should stand a while and infuse in hot water, which is then strained off and fresh water placed on the fire.
For 2 quarts berries take 3 quarts water.
The berries must be cooked well out and often stirred from the bottom, after which the jelly is made with sugar and cinnamon.
Light powdered sugar can well be used for gooseberry jelly, but white sugar gives finer taste and prettier appearance.

Alternatively, the berries can be cooked without letting them extract first; more water is taken for the same portion of berries, and as it thereby becomes too thin, it is smoothed with a couple of spoonfuls of corn-starch dissolved in cold water.
This saves both berries and sugar.
A third way is to take more berries and not let them cook quite to jelly, but strain them when it is like a purée.
The juice is then placed over again, made with sugar and cinnamon, and smoothed with corn-starch.
Gooseberries kept in bottles can also be used for jelly, but always need a thickening of corn-starch as they lose the jelly-like quality by being kept.

title: Stor Iskage (Large Ice Cake)
description: A cake made with powdered sugar, egg whites, and eggs.

ingredients.name: Equal weight of very finely powdered sugar

steps: Weigh 12 eggs, and take the same weight of each of the following: butter, very finely powdered sugar, and flour.
Beat the egg yolks and sugar together in a large bowl until it becomes a white salve.
Stir the flour into it and finally the butter, which has first been melted and somewhat cooled.
Beat the whites until white foam and blend with the rest.

Butter 8 to 10 pieces of paper of the size the ice cake should have, and spread a finger-thick layer of the batter on them, with a suitable opening in the middle so the baked cake has the form of a fairly broad wreath.
When the cakes are baked, take them from the paper and lay them on top of each other.
Beat 7 to 8 egg whites until foam and blend with the same number of tablespoons of sifted sugar, and brush the cakes with this both on the sides and on top.
Put it in a moderately warm oven to dry and lay it on the serving dish.
Immediately before serving, fill the opening in the middle with vanilla ice cream (Recipe 413).

title: Stor Kringle (Large Kringle)
description: Prepared with yeast, margarine, and cream.

steps: Mix yeast with salt
Knead together cardamom, eggs, margarine, flour and thin cream

Mix the dough the evening before, place in a cloth and bind with a band, but so that the dough has ample space to rise during the night
Place the cloth with the dough in a bowl or crock with ample cold water and set until the next morning
On the baking board place a little flour and pour out the dough, which with a light hand is rolled into a sausage

title: Stor Vol au vent (Large Vol au vent)
description: Prepared with puff pastry and egg white.
steps: Roll out two sheets of puff pastry to just under 1 centimeter (1/4 inch) thick.

As the dough shrinks during baking, the dough must be at least 1.5 centimeters (1/2 inch) larger in circumference than the measurement.
Place the thinner sheet of pastry on a baking sheet and brush with egg white.

Cut the second, slightly thicker sheet into a ring approximately 5 to 6 centimeters (2 inches) wide, and place it on top of the base sheet and brush with egg as well, but ensure nothing gets on the edges.
Cut the remaining dough into small strips or decorative figures; bake these together with the vol au vent in a well-heated oven and use them for garnishing.
When the puff pastry is to be a nice light brown, it is often necessary to turn the vol au vent so that it bakes evenly.

title: Straßburger Gäseleverpâté (Strasbourg Goose Liver Pâté)
description: Prepared with goose liver, pork fat, and truffles.
steps: Clean the truffles well, peel and cut into thick slices, then the shell is finely chopped.

Remove any spots carefully, and 1/2 pound of the goose liver is pounded into a fine farce with an equal amount of pork fat, an onion, a spoonful of parsley, the truffle shells and a little of the seasonings.
Cut the rest of the liver into 6 to 8 pieces, which are larded with slices of truffle that have been previously fried in butter with the rest of the onion and parsley.

Line the bottom of a fairly tall, cylindrical cooking vessel of porcelain or faience with thin slices of butter, over it a finger-thick layer of farce, then the larded slices of liver, which are sprinkled with seasonings, then another finger-thick layer of farce, thin slices of butter, and on top slices of pork fat. Cover the cooking vessel with paper and a lid, place on a baking sheet and bake in the oven for 2.5 to 3 hours.
Remove the paper and the pork fat slices.
Fill the cooking vessel completely with goose or pork offal, and a paper is placed anew under the lid.
Keeps for a long time in a cool place. All butter and offal used should be unsalted.

title: Sukat af Græskar eller Agurker (Candied Pumpkin or Cucumber)
description: Prepared with pumpkin or cucumbers, vinegar, and sugar.

ingredients.name: Pumpkin or large cucumbers, still green

steps: Cut into large pieces, give one boiling in water, and place on a clean cloth to dry. The outer skin should remain on, where it is not on the pumpkin too thick and hard
Dark powdered sugar is moistened with so much vinegar that it can melt; it is cooked until it is skimmed and clear, with 1 teaspoon ground ginger to each 2 pounds
Now the pieces are given a good boiling in the sugar, upon which they are taken up, placed in a crock, and the sauce is poured over warm. If it does not stand over, then more must be cooked

Since the pieces tend to float up, press them down with a tablespoon or a small round plate that is placed in the crock with some weight on it. After 8 days take them up to place the top ones at the bottom. When they have stood until you can taste that they are penetrated with sugar, they are taken up and placed in a dry crock or a deep vessel, and covered between each layer with dry powdered sugar

This also becomes syrup, and both this and the first can be used to candy other pumpkins with. The candied pieces are now placed in a light press between two large spoons with paper over and under. When they are pressed, thread a string through them and let them hang in an airy place to dry, but not in the sun
Finally place them in a crock with ground white sugar between each layer. The fruit must not be cooked too tender

title: Sukat af Meloner (Candied Melon)
description: Prepared with melon, white sugar, and water.
steps: Peel the melon, remove the seeds, and cut into finger-length pieces, about one inch wide and half as thick.
Weigh the pieces and place in a brine that is strong enough to float an egg; let sit for 4 days.
Remove the pieces and soak in cold water for 3 days, changing the water daily.
Place on heat in cold water and cook covered until tender enough to pierce with a stick; remove and dry thoroughly in cloth.
For 1 pound of melon, take 1 pound white sugar and cook with one-third pint water to make a syrup.
Add the melon to the syrup, cook for 5 to 6 minutes, pour into a jar and cover; let stand for 4 days.
Pour off the syrup, cook it for a few minutes, and pour hot over the melon; let stand for three days.
Spread on a sieve to drain for a few hours, then place on a plate.
Cook the syrup again until thick enough to pour over the melon; turn the melon in it and let stand several days in an airy place to dry.
Store in a dry place.

description: A soup made with vegetable stock, carrots, and turnips.
steps: Cut 4 carrots and 4 turnips into small cubes and cook until tender in some of the stock together with 1/2 L (1/2 pot) shelled peas.

title: Sure Valnødder til Saucer (Sour Walnuts for Sauces)
description: A sauce made with walnuts, vinegar, and shallots.

ingredients.name: Walnuts, picked at same time and of same size as preserved walnuts

steps: The walnuts are placed in a cold brine which is so strong that it can bear an egg, and must be fresh and well stirred. They stand in this for 6 days, are taken out and placed in a fresh and equally strong, cold brine, in which they again stand for 6 days
Strain them through a sieve where the brine is well drained, and place in a crock

Then place on the fire so much vinegar that it completely stands over the walnuts; to this for 100 walnuts add 4 shallots, a small piece of garlic, 3 pieces of ginger, 2 pieces of thin horseradish, 5 to 6 pieces of nutmeg, 10 cloves, 6 tablespoons whole mustard seed, 2 tablespoons pepper and 2 tablespoons mixed spices
When all this has boiled, strain it, cover with a cloth and pour cold over the walnuts, which are then tied up very securely, as air would make them soft
After a year they are ready to use and keep for several years. They are quite dark in color, but give a pure taste to sauce, especially in melted butter

title: Sursteg (Sour Roast)
description: Prepared with beef, vinegar, and beer.

ingredients.name: A good slice of butter or Palmin

steps: Beat the meat well with a meat mallet and rub with a mixture of salt, ground pepper and a little cloves.
Place the meat in a marinade of 1/4 L (1 pægl) vinegar, 1 L (1 pot) beer, a few whole peppercorns, 3 bay leaves and 2 onions sliced into slices for 3 to 4 days and turn regularly.
Brown a good slice of butter or Palmin in a pot, and place the meat in it after the marinade has drained well.
When sufficiently brown, pour in water and a little soy sauce or color.
Baste the roast regularly with the gravy, turn it and roast very slowly covered for 2.5 to 3 hours.
Strain the gravy and skim the fat.
In the fat that is skimmed, brown flour for the sauce and dilute with the gravy and season with salt, a little sugar, currant juice and color if necessary.
Boiled potatoes can be served alongside.

title: Sv eder med Eddike til Steg (Quinces with Vinegar for Serving)

title: Svensk Knækbrød (Swedish Crisp Bread)
description: A bread preparation made with wheat flour, yeast, and caraway seeds.

ingredients.name: half wheat flour and half rye flour

steps: Place 2 measures sweet milk and 1/2 pound butter over heat and warm.
Work half wheat flour and half rye flour with 2 measures good yeast together into a dough and knead well until it begins to rise.
Add more flour and two handfuls caraway seeds and knead with the hands until the dough releases from the hands and the dough trough.
Let it rise.
When it has risen, punch it down.
Roll out a piece of dough the size of a goose egg to the thickness of a straw, trim the edges with a pastry wheel and prick with a fork so it does not puff up during baking.
Let the cakes rise further and bake in the oven at good heat.
Store in a dry place.
